purpose: Whether GovKit's Storybook can expose an MCP endpoint for design-tool discovery, checked against the registry and the repository rather than release notes
question: Can @storybook/addon-mcp be connected to GovKit's Storybook without an infrastructure change?
answer: No. Not because of the Storybook version, which was the earlier assumption, but because every published version of the addon takes @storybook/addon-vitest as a hard peer and GovKit tests with jest.

govkit.source: package.json of the gov-ui-kit worktree at 8d70bdf0c7fc32e994894d47067f518253b04f80

corrections: An earlier working note recorded that connecting the addon requires a Storybook 10.6 bump because the first stable release is 10.6.0. That is wrong: 0.7.0 accepts storybook ^10.5.0-0, which GovKit's ^10.5.7 satisfies, so the Storybook minor is not the blocker.

The blocker is @storybook/addon-vitest, a hard peer in every published version including 0.7.0. GovKit runs jest and has neither vitest nor addon-vitest, so connecting the addon means introducing a second test runner into the kit.

relatedEvidence.publicStorybook: SUPERSEDED by access/storybook-hosted.json. The earlier note here cited access/storybook.json to claim there is no hosted Storybook. That check probed https://aragon.github.io/gov-ui-kit/, which does 404, but is not the hosted site. GovKit's Storybook is live at https://uikit.aragon.org/, serving index.json (v5, 441 entries) and project.json (storybook 10.5.7, @storybook/react-vite) as static files.

conclusion: A public MCP endpoint is not reachable without adding Vitest to GovKit AND permanently running `storybook dev`, because /mcp is dev-server middleware (experimental_devServer with app.get/app.post in the addon's preset) and cannot exist in a static build. It is also not needed for discovery: the hosted index.json already enumerates every story statically, and the registry plus selection guide carry App usage and evidence-backed intent that a manifest does not. If a machine-readable manifest is still wanted, componentsManifest is a build artifact and would ship from the same static host without a server or Vitest.
